description: What each Claude Code hook behaviour becomes on the other runtimes. `ported` runs the same shared decision; `equivalent` is a runtime-native hook covering the same need differently; `unverified` runs the same shared decision from a hook built from the runtime's documentation that no live run has yet shown to deny; `not-ported` has no counterpart, with the reason. An `antigravity` row is `ported` only with a `probe` record ({ date, observed: "deny", by }) of a live run in which it denied. Every safety behaviour and every handler in handlers.json appears once. A handler cell other than `not-ported` names its hook in `where.<runtime>`, an `unverified` one cites its source in `notes.<runtime>`, and a hook a runtime ships with no Claude Code counterpart is listed under `runtimeOnly`. Checked by the tests in the kit's source repository.

codex.note: Codex has no file-read hook; the decision runs on the shell command and the paths it names. The archived-plan read gate runs on the command: a read, list or search command naming a path under tasks/plans/archive/.

cursor.note: The credential-file and archived-plan read rules also run in .cursor/hooks/shell-gate.cjs (beforeShellExecution) on the files a command names, and the archived-plan rule in .cursor/hooks/tool-gate.cjs for search and list tools; in those two gates the kill switch downgrades them.

grok.note: A hook Grok stops at its timeout lets the call through, and so does a shell command carried under a field name the guard does not know.

pi.note: Pi lets a call run when an extension throws, so the extension catches every failure and blocks.

antigravity.note: From documentation (https://antigravity.google/docs/hooks, read 2026-11-22); no live run has shown it deny. The page does not say what the host does with a hook it stops at its timeout or one that exits without a decision.

cursor.note: When Cursor also loads the Claude Code hooks, a per-command marker makes the check run once.

grok.note: Where Claude Code is installed too, Grok also runs the hooks in .claude/settings.json; both use the same per-command marker.

omp.where: .agents/meowkit/hooks/guard.cjs (hook module .omp/hooks/pre/meowkit.ts, tool_call on a shell command)
omp.note: With the claude provider left on, OMP also loads hook modules under .claude/hooks/pre; the kit has none there.

antigravity.note: From documentation (https://antigravity.google/docs/hooks, read 2026-11-22); no live run has shown it deny. A check with no verdict answers force_ask; the registration's 300 s timeout sits above the checks' 270 s deadline because the host's timeout behaviour is not documented.

pre-completion-check.reason: Opt-in. Cursor: stop-followup.cjs returns the reason as followup_message. Pi and OMP: agent_end runs .agents/meowkit/hooks/completion.cjs and sends the reason as a follow-up message that starts another turn. All use lib/core/completion-check.cjs; its cap of two blocks per session is the loop guard where the host passes none. Grok and Antigravity document a Stop continuation, but the shape of their shell results is not confirmed, so no pass could be recorded there yet. Codex: not run, because no passing check can be recorded there (see verification-evidence); a Stop block would continue every turn that changed files.

notes.pi: https://github.com/earendil-works/pi docs/extensions.md at 1.7.0 (tool_result, agent_end, sendMessage) and packages/coding-agent/src/core/tools/bash.ts:444-452 (isError and structuredContent.exit_code on a failing exit); no live run yet.
notes.omp: Probed 2026-11-28 on OMP 19.2.1 in an RPC session: an edit with no check got the follow-up, which started a new run; its passing npm test was recorded and the next agent_end let the turn end. omp -p (print mode) exits before the follow-up is sent, so a print-mode run gets no reminder. Source: @oh-my-pi/pi-coding-agent 18.13.3 src/extensibility/hooks/types.ts, src/tools/bash.ts:722-761.

plan-state-sync.reason: Always on. Codex: .codex/hooks/completion-check.cjs on Stop syncs and adds the line as systemMessage. Cursor: stop-followup.cjs syncs and writes the line to stderr (stop has no user-visible message field). Pi and OMP: agent_end runs .agents/meowkit/hooks/completion.cjs, which syncs, and the extension shows the line with ctx.ui.notify. Grok and Antigravity have no Stop hook the kit uses: the ship check prints the same drift line read-only and the agent runs mewkit plan sync. All use lib/core/plan-state-sync.cjs.

verification-evidence.reason: Cursor: completion-check.cjs on postToolUse Shell (success only). Pi and OMP: a bash tool_result the runtime reports as a success (isError false, and no failing exit code) runs .agents/meowkit/hooks/completion.cjs, which records the pass. Codex: PostToolUse for the shell tool carries tool_response as the output text only, with no exit code (codex-rs 0.120 through 0.142 and later), so a hook cannot tell a passing command from a failing one.

cursor..cursor/hooks/mcp-gate.cjs: beforeMCPExecution: allowlist for MCP calls (lib/mcp-allowlist-policy.cjs), fail-closed. Claude Code has no MCP gate in the kit.
cursor..cursor/hooks/subagent-lifecycle.cjs: subagentStart and subagentStop: a bounded, scrubbed status record and a follow-up when a subagent ended in error. Advisory; Claude Code's SubagentStop registers no kit handler.

nodeMissing.claude-code: Not probed. A registration whose `node` cannot start fails like any non-2 exit, which Claude Code treats as non-blocking.
nodeMissing.codex: Not probed. Codex documents exit 2 and the deny JSON as blocks; a spawn failure is not documented. Needs a maintainer run with node removed from PATH.
nodeMissing.cursor: Not probed. Every blocking registration sets failClosed: true, which Cursor documents as blocking on hook failure; confirm with node removed from PATH.
nodeMissing.grok: Not probed. Grok documents every hook failure but an explicit deny as fail-open, so a `node` that cannot start lets the call through.
nodeMissing.pi: Not probed. The extension runs `node` through `pi.exec` and blocks the call when it gets no answer, so a `node` that cannot start blocks every tool call.
nodeMissing.omp: Not probed. The hook module runs `node` through `pi.exec` and blocks the call when it gets no answer, so a `node` that cannot start blocks every tool call.
nodeMissing.antigravity: Not probed. The hooks page documents only a stdout decision; what the host does when the command fails to start, exits without output or runs past its timeout is not stated, so a `node` that cannot start may let the call through.
